evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.36: corpora juvenum firmārī labōre voluērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Strengthen a body, a wall, a position, a resolve; to make lasting or secure.

evidence: Caes. BG 6.21: hōc vīrēs nervōsque cōnfirmārī putant (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Strengthen in body or in mind (cōnfirmā tē, take heart); also confirm, assert, and encourage. sē cōnfirmāre is to recover after an illness.

evidence: Cic. Cael. 11: cum is jam sē corrōborāvisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From rōbur: to give strength to a growing body or a virtue; sē corrōborāre is to grow up and grow strong.

phrases.latin: et discās oportet et quod didicistī agendō cōnfirmēs
phrases.english: you must learn, and strengthen what you have learned by doing it

sources: Lewis & Short: firmo · Lewis & Short: confirmo · Lewis & Short: corroboro
